name: Handlebar moustache

card.summary: A moustache with long ends that curl upward like bicycle handlebars, grown and waxed to add a distinctive, groomed look to the face.
card.note: Needs regular grooming; without it the shape can resemble a walrus moustache.

quick.overview:
A handlebar moustache is a facial hair style with long ends that curl upward. Men grow it to give the face a defined, characterful look, framing the mouth and adding visual weight to the upper lip.

It has been worn since antiquity, popular among 19th-century soldiers and Wild West figures, revived by baseball pitcher Rollie Fingers in 1972, and adopted by hipster culture. Research on moustaches in general has found mixed perceptions of wearers.
quick.how: The style is usually achieved by growing the moustache long and shaping the ends with moustache wax; hair gel, a curling iron or natural curl can also work. The greater the curl at the ends, the more dramatic the look.
quick.risks: There are no medical risks beyond ordinary skin irritation from grooming products. Perception varies by audience: some studies found moustached men rated more favourably by hiring managers, others found preference for clean-shaven men.

lead: The handlebar moustache is a moustache with long ends that curl upward, resembling bicycle handlebars. People grow it to add a distinctive focal point to the lower face, a polished retro or vintage look that depends on grooming. [1]

Similar moustaches appear in depictions of Iron Age Celts, and European soldiers commonly wore the style until about World War I. In the United States it was popular in the late 1800s, among figures such as Wyatt Earp. [1]
In 1972 Oakland A's pitcher Rollie Fingers grew one to win a $300 prize for best facial hair offered by owner Charlie Finley, and kept it for his career. Hipster subculture later adopted it. [1]

chain: Shape the ends upward with wax
angle.text: Grooming turns facial hair into a deliberate style element. Wax or gel holds the curled ends in place, giving a defined shape rather than a walrus-like drooping moustache.

infobox: Moustache wax, gel or curling iron

paras: The handlebar is distinguished by long ends that curl upward, and is sometimes called a spaghetti moustache, a nickname tied to stereotypes of Italian men. [1] Other moustache styles include the horseshoe, Fu Manchu, pencil and walrus. [2]
Moustaches appear in Ancient Egyptian art, and Iron Age Celts wore them. Western popularity peaked in the 1880s and 1890s with an emphasis on military virtues. [2]

Comedian Jimmy Edwards grew one in the late 1940s to hide facial injuries from his time as a World War II pilot. Notable wearers include Wilhelm II, Buffalo Bill, Bhagat Singh and William Howard Taft, and brand mascots such as Mr. Monopoly and Julius Pringles. [1]

A study of hiring managers found men with moustaches or beards rated higher than clean-shaven men, while a Brazilian study found clean-shaven men preferred. Muscarella and Cunningham found moustached men seen as older and more aggressive; women's preferences varied across studies. [2]
No studies found. A 1982 plastic surgery paper uses the name 'handlebar' for a breast reduction incision technique, which is unrelated to the facial hair style.

timeline.event: Jimmy Edwards grows one after wartime injuries. [1]
Rollie Fingers wins a facial hair prize and keeps the handlebar. [1]
